items.title: On the Strait of Hormuz, BBC finds seized ships and shark fishermen as uneasy calm returns
items.description: The BBC travels to the city of Bandar Abbas - the first international journalists to visit the Iranian side of the strait.

items.title: Venezuela quake survivor pulled out alive after eight days
items.description: Hernán Gil was trapped under a collapsed multi-storey car park.

items.title: At least 32 dead after overcrowded bus plunges into ravine in Pakistan
items.description: The bus was travelling from Quetta to Peshawar, when it crashed in the Dana Sar mountain range.

items.title: Instagram running ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India, BBC finds
items.description: The ads use terms including “rape” and “child video” and link to content on the messaging app Telegram.

items.title: Taylor Swift's rumoured wedding celebrations begin with star-studded New York event
items.description: Actress Lena Dunham, model Gigi Hadid and longtime music collaborator Jack Antonoff were spotted in formal attire near Madison Square Garden.

items.title: 'Most massive' Russian attack on Kyiv kills at least 30
items.description: The latest barrage deployed the largest number of weapons on the capital and hit locations over a wide area.

items.title: Iran begins public mourning for Ayatollah killed in February
items.description: Ali Khamenei's body will lie in state in Tehran's Grand Mosalla from Friday ahead of days-long funeral events.

items.title: A mayor in Japan announced her maternity leave - and got the whole country talking
items.description: In the face of criticism, Shoko Kawata, 35, says she loves her job and is proud to be taking time off to have a baby.

items.title: Bomb blast at Damascus cafe kills nine, Syrian state media say
items.description: There was no immediate claim for the bombing at a cafe close to the Palace of Justice, a major government building.

items.title: Ebola treatments trial begins in DR Congo
items.description: According to WHO data, there have been 1,406 confirmed cases of the disease in DRC, with 301 suspected cases and 438 deaths.

items.title: Killers of British couple in South Africa sentenced to life
items.description: The pair had been collecting rare plants and seeds before their bodies were found days later in a river.

items.title: Canadian boy, 11, dies of rabies after waking to bat on his face
items.description: Rabies infections are rare in Canada. There have been 28 human deaths due to rabies in the country since 1924.
